To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spin and charge are localized in radical 11 but are delocalized in the other radicals studied.
the magnetic properties of the phenalenyl radicals result from the delocalization of the spin in the crystal lattice.

(1) the magnetic properties of phenalenyl radical-based molecular conductors are determined by the degree of localization or delocalization of the electronic structure, (2) the magnetic phase transitions in the dimer and pi-chain conductors are accompanied by a dramatic increase in conductivity that is due to the formation of an extended electronic structure, and (3) the pi-dimer radicals are diamagnetic in the solid-state.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of the first experimentally based structural model of the electronic structure in a class of organic conductors that has been the subject of intense theoretical investigation for over two decades.
the development of the chemistry of neutral radicals and their application to the development of novel organic materials.
the synthesis of new neutral radical molecular conductive materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the phenalenyl radical-based neutral radical conductive materials are not diamagnetic pi-dimers, but rather are highly delocalized molecular conductors.
the phenalenyl radical and its derivatives are not simple, localized, organic free radicals, but rather are highly delocalized, organic, molecular conductors.
the spin is localized in all of the phenalenyl based radicals that we have examined, and the charge is delocalized in the monomeric and pi-chain radicals but is localized in the dimer radicals.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the phenalenyl neutral radicals that we have studied have a strong preference to remain in a delocalized electronic state and only in the case of the dimeric radicals is there evidence for the formation of a localized electronic structure.
the neutral radicals that have the strongest pi-donor/acceptor character and the highest pi-electron densities (i.e., radicals 4,12, and 14) are the most localized in the crystal.

the spin and charge remain delocalized throughout the series of neutral radical conductors, but the delocalization is enhanced at the magnetic transition in the dimers and in the pi-chain radicals, and is reduced in the monomers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spin and charge are highly localized in all the neutral radical molecular conductive materials we have studied.

the degree of delocalization of the electronic structure is strongly correlated with the magnitude of the conductivity in the radical and that the conductivity in the dithiophene radical (2) and the ethyl (1), butyl (3), and phenyl (5) dimers is due to an enhanced delocalization of their electronic structure.

the electronic structure of the phenalenyl radicals is highly dependent on the crystal lattice environment and that the electronic structure can be manipulated by changing the molecular environment of the radical.
